what.description: WHAT happened - COMPLETE, DETAILED description with ALL specifics. NEVER summarize or omit details. Include: exact actions, objects, quantities, specifics. BE VERBOSE - capture every detail that was mentioned. Example: 'Emily got married to Sarah at a rooftop garden ceremony with 50 guests attending and a live jazz band playing' NOT: 'A wedding happened' or 'Emily got married'

when.description: WHEN it happened - ALWAYS include temporal information if mentioned. Include: specific dates, times, durations, relative time references. Examples: 'on June 15th, 2024 at 3pm', 'last weekend', 'for the past 3 years', 'every morning at 6am'. Write null ONLY if absolutely no temporal context exists. Prefer converting to absolute dates when possible.

where.description: WHERE it happened or is about - SPECIFIC locations, places, areas, regions if applicable. Include: cities, neighborhoods, venues, buildings, countries, specific addresses when mentioned. Examples: 'downtown San Francisco at a rooftop garden venue', 'at the user's home in Brooklyn', 'online via Zoom', 'Paris, France'. Write null ONLY if absolutely no location context exists or if the fact is completely location-agnostic.

who.description: WHO is involved - ALL people/entities with FULL context and relationships. Include: names, roles, relationships to user, background details. Resolve coreferences (if 'my roommate' is later named 'Emily', write 'Emily, the user's college roommate'). BE DETAILED about relationships and roles. Example: 'Emily (user's college roommate from Stanford, now works at Google), Sarah (Emily's partner of 5 years, software engineer)' NOT: 'my friend' or 'Emily and Sarah'

why.description: WHY it matters - ALL emotional, contextual, and motivational details. Include EVERYTHING: feelings, preferences, motivations, observations, context, background, significance. BE VERBOSE - capture all the nuance and meaning. FOR EXPERIENCE FACTS: MUST include what the user asked/requested that led to this interaction! Example (world): 'The user felt thrilled and inspired, has always dreamed of an outdoor ceremony, mentioned wanting a similar garden venue, was particularly moved by the intimate atmosphere and personal vows' Example (experience): 'User asked how to fix slow API performance with 1000+ concurrent users, expected 70-80% reduction in database load' NOT: 'User liked it' or 'To help user'

fact_kind.description: 'event' = specific datable occurrence (set occurred dates), 'conversation' = general info (no occurred dates)

fact_type.description: 'world' = objective/external facts about the user, other people, events, general knowledge, preferences, rules, corrections, or constraints. 'experience' = actions, experiences, or observations the assistant/agent actually performed (e.g., 'I changed X', 'I discovered Y').

occurred_start.description: WHEN the event happened (ISO 8601 timestamp). Only for fact_kind='event'. null for conversations.

occurred_end.description: WHEN the event ended (ISO 8601 timestamp). Only for fact_kind='event'. null for conversations.

time_expression.description: The temporal phrase exactly as the text wrote it (e.g. 'last spring'); null if none

entities.description: Named entities, objects, AND abstract concepts from the fact. Include: people names, organizations, places, significant objects (e.g., 'coffee maker', 'car'), AND abstract concepts/themes (e.g., 'friendship', 'career growth', 'loss', 'celebration'). Extract anything that could help link related facts together.

name.description: The entity as the text names it

kind.description: One lowercase word: person, organization, place, ...; null if unclear

labels.description: Classification labels as key/value pairs; [] when no label applies or none are configured

key.description: Label key, or 'group:field' for a structured entity field

caused_by.description: Causal links to PREVIOUS facts only: 0-based indexes, each MUST be less than this fact's position. Example: fact #3 can only reference facts 0, 1, or 2. Max 2 per fact; [] if none.
